title: Place value and rounding
blurb: Name every place from millions to ten-thousandths, read and write decimals in words, and round to any place correctly.
question: A lab balance shows 12.3456 g. Which digit is in the thousandths place, and what is the mass rounded to the nearest hundredth?

teach.body: Formally, in our base-ten system each place is worth 10 times the place to its right, so a digit's value depends on its position; rounding replaces a number with the nearest value at a chosen place. In plain English: know the name of every place, and round by looking at one digit only. On the HESI A2 the stem names the place (tenths, hundreds, nearest thousand), and the wrong options round to the place next door.

head: Place
Value
Digit
teach.caption: Commas group the whole-number side in threes; the decimal point sits between ones and tenths.

teach.h: Mirror names around the ones place
teach.caption: The names mirror around the ONES place, not the point: there is no "oneths" place. Listen for the -ths.

items: Say the whole number, say "and" for the point, read the decimal digits as one number, then name the LAST digit's place.
4.072 = four and seventy-two thousandths (the 2 sits in the thousandths place).
Zeros between digits matter: 0.05 is not 0.5. Zeros at the end do not: 3.08 = 3.080.
Underline the target place. Nearest tenth: the 4 in 3.462.
Look ONLY at the digit immediately to its right: 6.
5 or more: round the target digit up. 4 or less: keep it. 6 ≥ 5, so 4 becomes 5.
Drop the digits to the right (or make them zeros in a whole number): 3.5.
Check: 3.462 is past the halfway point 3.45, so 3.5 is nearer. ✓ Nearest hundredth: 3.46; nearest whole: 3.

head: Number
Round to
Result
teach.caption: When a 9 rounds up it becomes 10 and carries: 3.96 → 4.0, never 3.10.
The halfway point (3.45) itself rounds up.

teach.body: In a multi-step problem, keep full values until the final answer, then round once to the place the question asks for. Rounding early carries an error forward. Example: 2.47 × 3 = 7.41, which rounds to 7.4. Round 2.47 to 2.5 first and you get 7.5, a different answer. Only round early when the stem tells you to.

teach.text: Rounding slips the HESI A2 uses: rounding to the wrong place (tens instead of tenths, hundreds instead of hundredths), truncating instead of rounding (3.47 → 3.4 to the nearest tenth; it is 3.5), rounding in stages from the far right (0.0749 → 0.075 → 0.08; it is 0.07), and botching a 9 (3.96 → 3.10; it is 4.0).

teach.body: Marisol Ortiz, a pharmacy-technician applicant, weighs a powder at 12.3456 g. Places after the point: 3 tenths, 4 hundredths, 5 thousandths, 6 ten-thousandths. To the nearest hundredth she looks only at the thousandths digit, 5, so the 4 rounds up: 12.35 g. To the nearest tenth she looks at the 4, so the 3 stays: 12.3 g. Check: 12.3456 is past 12.345, the halfway point between 12.34 and 12.35. ✓

items: Whole places: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands … millions. Decimal places: tenths, hundredths, thousandths, ten-thousandths.
Read a decimal by the place of its last digit; say "and" for the point.
Look at the one digit right of the target place: 5 or more rounds up, 4 or less keeps.
A 9 that rounds up carries into the next place (3.96 → 4.0).
Round once, at the end, to the place the question names.

summary: You can now name every place from millions to ten-thousandths, read and write decimals in words, and round to any place, carrying correctly through 9s and rounding only at the end. You also spot the next-door-place and truncation options the HESI A2 offers.

A.why: The hundredths digit is 8. The next digit is 6 (5 or more), so round up: 47.09.

whyNot.0: 47.08 truncates (cuts off) the digits instead of rounding; the 6 means round up.
whyNot.2: 47.1 rounds to the nearest tenth, the wrong place.
whyNot.3: 47.086 rounds to the nearest thousandth, the wrong place.

A.q: In 7,463,215.08, which digit is in the hundred-thousands place?
A.why: From the left: 7 millions, 4 hundred thousands, 6 ten thousands, 3 thousands. The hundred-thousands digit is 4.

whyNot.2: 8 is in the hundredths place, on the decimal side (note the -ths).

A.why: The decimal digits read as 307, and the last digit (7) is in the fourth place, ten-thousandths: three hundred seven ten-thousandths.

whyNot.0: Three hundred seven thousandths is 0.307; the 7 in 0.0307 is one place farther right.
whyNot.2: Thirty-seven ten-thousandths is 0.0037; it drops the 0 between the 3 and the 7.

B.q: A patient's temperature reads 99.85°F. What is this rounded to the nearest tenth?
B.why: The tenths digit is 8 and the next digit is 5. 5 or more rounds up, so 99.9°F.

whyNot.0: 99.8°F rounds a 5 down; a 5 rounds up.
whyNot.2: 100.0°F rounds to the nearest whole degree, the wrong place.
whyNot.3: 99.0°F cuts off everything after the ones place.

B.q: Which number rounds to 5.7 when rounded to the nearest tenth?
B.why: In 5.65 the tenths digit is 6 and the next digit is 5, so it rounds up to 5.7.

whyNot.0: 5.649 has a 4 after the tenths digit, so it rounds down to 5.6.

B.why: A zero added after the last decimal digit does not change the value: 3.08 = 3.080 (8 hundredths either way).

whyNot.1: 3.80 moves the 8 into the tenths place: 8 tenths, not 8 hundredths.
whyNot.2: 3.008 moves the 8 into the thousandths place.
whyNot.3: 30.8 moves the decimal point one place right (10 times as large).

C.q: A recipe uses 1.375 cups of oats per batch. How many cups are needed for 7 batches? Round your answer to the nearest tenth.
C.why: Keep full values, round at the end: 1.375 × 7 = 9.625. The digit after the tenths is 2, so 9.6.

whyNot.0: 9.8 rounds 1.375 to 1.4 first (1.4 × 7), carrying the rounding error.
whyNot.1: 9.7 rounds 1.375 to 1.38 first (1.38 × 7 = 9.66), then rounds again.
whyNot.3: 9.63 rounds to the nearest hundredth, not the nearest tenth.

C.q: A dose works out to 0.4962 mL, and the syringe is marked in hundredths of a milliliter. What volume is drawn up, to the nearest hundredth?
C.why: The hundredths digit is 9 and the next digit is 6, so the 9 rounds up to 10 and carries into the tenths: 0.4962 → 0.50 mL.

whyNot.0: 0.410 writes the rounded 9 as "10" without carrying it into the tenths place.
whyNot.1: 0.49 truncates; the 6 after the 9 means round up.
whyNot.3: 0.496 rounds to the nearest thousandth, the wrong place.

C.q: A hospital system recorded 1,486,512 patient visits last year. What is this number rounded to the nearest ten thousand?
C.why: The ten-thousands digit is 8 (1,4[8]6,512). The next digit is 6, so round up to 9 and zero the rest: 1,490,000.

whyNot.0: 1,480,000 truncates; the 6 to the right means round up.
whyNot.2: 1,500,000 rounds to the nearest hundred thousand, the wrong place.
whyNot.3: 1,487,000 rounds to the nearest thousand, the wrong place.

reteach.title: Rounding is choosing the nearer exit
reteach.question: You are driving between highway exits 40 and 50 and you are at mile 47. Which exit is nearer, and how does that picture explain the rounding rule?

blocks.body: At mile 47 you are 7 miles past exit 40 and 3 miles before exit 50, so exit 50 is nearer: 47 rounds to 50. At mile 45 you are exactly halfway, and the rule says take the exit ahead: 45 rounds up to 50. The place you round to sets how far apart the exits are: nearest ten means exits every 10 miles, nearest tenth means exits every 0.1 mile.

items: 3.462 to the nearest tenth: the "exits" are 3.4 and 3.5, halfway is 3.45.
3.462 is past 3.45, so it rounds to 3.5.
Only the digit right after the target place (6) decides; later digits don't matter.

blocks.text: Cutting a number off is not rounding: mile 47 is not "exit 40" just because it starts with a 4.

explain.body: Count from the ones place outward. Left of the point: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands. Right of the point: tenths, hundredths, thousandths, ten-thousandths.

test.q: In 3,048.2617, what is the place of the digit 6?
test.why: Right of the point: 2 tenths, 6 hundredths, 1 thousandth, 7 ten-thousandths. The 6 is in the hundredths place.

whyNot.0: Hundreds is a whole-number place; the hundreds digit of 3,048 is 0.
whyNot.1: Tenths is the first place after the point, which holds the 2.
whyNot.3: Thousandths is the third place after the point, which holds the 1.

explain.body: Look only at the digit immediately right of the target place. Never round in stages from the far right: 0.0749 to the nearest hundredth looks at the 4, so it stays 0.07.

test.why: The hundredths digit is 7; the digit after it is 4, so keep the 7: 0.07.

whyNot.0: 0.08 rounds in stages (0.0749 → 0.075 → 0.08); only the digit right after the target counts.

explain.body: When the target digit is 9 and it rounds up, it becomes 10: write 0 and add 1 to the place on its left, just like carrying in addition.

test.why: The tenths digit is 9 and the next digit is 6, so the 9 rounds up to 10: write 0 tenths and carry 1 into the ones, 19 → 20. Answer 20.0.

whyNot.0: 19.9 truncates; the 6 after the 9 means round up.
whyNot.1: 19.10 writes the rounded 9 as "10" without carrying into the ones place.
whyNot.3: 19.0 turns the 9 into 0 but forgets to carry 1 into the ones place.

explain.body: Carry full values through every step, then round the final answer once. 3.45 × 2.8 = 9.66, which rounds to 9.7.

test.q: Compute 3.45 × 2.8. Round your answer to the nearest tenth.
test.why: 3.45 × 2.8 = 9.66. The digit after the tenths is 6, so round up: 9.7.

whyNot.2: 9.66 is not rounded to the nearest tenth.
